The increasing width of the 90% confidence intervals directly corresponds to the growing uncertainty associated with longer forecast horizons. Conversely, a severe economic downturn, a significant operational failure, an unforeseen negative market disruption from a competitor, or a sudden adverse change in policy could cause the metric to fall below the lower bound. These "black swan" events, by their very nature, are difficult to quantify within standard probabilistic forecasts but represent the primary risks for outcomes outside the stated 90% confidence ranges.
